body.p: This Amendment is responsive to the Office Action dated April 12, 2023. Applicant has amended claims 1, 11, 13, 21 and 22 and canceled claims 6 and 7. Claims 1 - 5 and 8 -22 remain pending upon entry of this communication.

Applicant would like to thank Examiner Berhanu for discussing the Office Action during the Applicant-initiated telephonic interview conducted on 12 July 2023. Examiner Berhanu and Applicant's representative Adrian Sanchez (Reg. No. 75, 159), participated in the interview.During the telephonic interview, Examiner Berhanu and Applicant's representatives discussed the rejection of claim 1 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over U.S. Patent Application Publication No. 2009/0082691 by Denison et al. (hereinafter, "Denison 691") in view of U.S. Patent Application Publication No. 2007/0197930 by Sarkela (hereinafter, "Sarkela"), as evidenced by U.S. Patent 5,601,090 to Musha (hereinafter "Musha"). The participants further discussed the rejection 35 U.S.C. § 112(a). The participants also discussed the prosecution history, which was crossed off on the IDS filed 1 July 2021. The Examiner noted that Examiner's will automatically consider the prosecution history. To avoid having the prosecution history crossed off, Applicant may list individual file history items in an IDS. No agreements were reached. No exhibits were introduced, and no demonstrations were conducted during the interview.
In the Office Action, the Examiner noted that 35 U.S. C. 112(f) has been invoked when interpreting claim 21. Applicant acknowledges the interpretation of claim 21 under 35 U.S. C. 112(f).

In the Office Action, the Office rejected claims 1-22 under 35 U.S.C. 112(a) asserting that claims 1-22 are not supported by Applicant's specification. Specifically the Office stated, "the specification fails to provide adequate written description for ... one or more processors configured to select a first frequency band of interest and a second frequency band of interest,"

and that there "is no description of how a selected second frequency band would be incorporated into the method of determining a control signal for the therapy device."1 Applicant respectfully disagrees.
As one example, FIG. 9 and the associated description of FIG. 9 includes that a processor of Applicant's system:
receives a long term bioelectrical brain signal recording, [and the] length of the bioelectrical brain signal recording is selected such that the bioelectrical signal
sensed by sensing module 66 during at least two different patient states is
recorded ... Processor 80 may determine one or more frequency sub-bands and
one or more frequency bands of interest using any suitable technique. ...

referred to as
. By tracking of a

bioelectrical brain signal of patient 12 over relatively long periods of time (e.g., on the order of hours or even days), characteristics of the one or more frequency sub-band components indicative of one or more patient states may be observed.
... processor 80 may perform a power spectral analysis of the sensed bioelectrical
brain signal to determine one or more biomarkers (e.g., frequency sub-band
components)2 indicative of one or more patient states.... processor 80 of
programmer 14 or another processor, alone or with the aid of a clinician, may use
the one or more biomarkers to control therapy to maintain a threshold level of
activity in one or more particular frequency sub-bands or, depending on the
patient condition, to maintain a lack of activity in the one or more frequency sub- bands), or to achieve a particular change in the activity in the one or more
frequency sub-bands. In this way, the biomarkers may be used by processor 60 of
IMD 16 or another device to control closed-loop therapy.3

As shown by the excerpts above, Applicant's disclosure clearly discloses selecting one or more frequency bands and thus clearly discloses at least "selecting a first frequency band of interest of the bioelectrical brain signal from a plurality of predetermined frequency bands" and "selecting a second frequency band of interest of the bioelectrical brain signal." Applicant's disclosure further describes in details some examples of "how a selected second frequency band would be incorporated into the method of determining a control signal for the therapy device," for example in Applicant's paragraphs [0160] and [0161]. Moreover, the description of Applicant's FIG. 9 states "frequency sub-band components,"4 "one or more frequency sub-bands"5 and "frequency sub-bands of interest," which in Applicant's description of FIG. 9 were not limited to a single
1 NFOA dated 2023-04-12 at page 5, section 6.

2 The "frequency sub-band components" in this sentence need not be limited to a single "frequency band of interest," but instead may be sub-bands of any of the "one or more frequency bands of interest."
3 See e.g., Applicant's FIG. 9 and paragraphs [0154] - [0161].
4 See e.g., Applicant's paragraph [0159].
s See e.g., Applicant's paragraph [0161].

frequency band of interest and would not have been interpreted by one of ordinary skill in the art to be limited to only a single frequency band, especially in light of the phrase "one or more frequency bands of interest," throughout Applicant's description.

Applicant submits that claims 1 - 22 are supported by Applicant's specification, in accordance with 35 U.S.C. 112(a). Similar arguments apply to the Examiner's assertion regarding the priority date of the Application. For example, the originally filed provisional application also describes that the processor "may determine one or more frequency sub-bands and one or more frequency bands of interest using any suitable technique," in the description of FIG. 9. Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration withdrawal of the rejections under 35 U.S.C. 112(a) as well as acceptance of Applicant's claim for benefit of the prior-filed application.
The Office Action rejected claims 1 - 22 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as follows:
" Claims 1-6, 9-16, and 19-22 were rejected as allegedly being unpatentable over
"Denison et al.'691, in view of Sarkela, and in further view of Musha; and
" Claims 7, 8, 17, and 18 were rejected as allegedly being unpatentable over Denison et
al.'691, in view of Sarkela (as evidenced by Musha), and in further view of U.S. Patent
Application Publication No. 2008/0228100 by Navakatikyan (hereinafter,
"Navakatikyan").

Without conceding the merits of the rejection, Applicant has amended the claims solely to advance prosecution towards allowance. Applicant respectfully traverses the rejections to the extent the rejections may be considered applicable to the claims as amended. The applied references, alone or in any combination, do not disclose the features defined by Applicant's claims, and there would have been no apparent reason that would have caused one of ordinary skill in the art to modify the applied references to arrive at the claimed features.
The cited references, in any reasonable combination, do not disclose the subject matter of Applicant's independent claim 1, specifically:
determining a first biomarker indicative of a first patient state by, after selecting
the first set of two or more frequency sub-bands, at least determining a first
characteristic of the bioelectrical brain signal within the two or more frequency
sub-bands of the first set indicative of the first patient state, wherein the first
characteristic comprises a predetermined characteristic of a distribution of a signal
strength within the two or more frequency sub-bands of the first set, and wherein
the predetermined characteristic of the distribution comprises one or more of a
peak width less than or equal to a first threshold value, a peak width greater than
or equal to a second threshold value.

Although not identical in scope, independent claims 11, 21, and 22 as amended include subject matter similar to those discussed above for claim 1, and the arguments presented with respect to claim 1 can be considered equally applicable to claims 11, 21, and 22.
For at least the reasons discussed above, independent claims 1, 11, 21, and 22 are

patentable over the cited references. The dependent claims incorporate the requirements of the respective independent claims.6 Accordingly, the dependent claims are likewise patentable. Applicant therefore respectfully requests reconsideration and withdrawal of the rejections under 35 U.S.C. § 103.
All claims in this application are in condition for allowance. Applicant does not

acquiesce as to any assertion in the Office Action with respect to the cited art or to Applicant's claims. Applicant's silence with respect to any assertion in the Office Action should not be interpreted as Applicant's acquiescence thereto. Applicant reserves the right to comment further with respect to the applied references and any pending claim in a future Amendment, Response, or on appeal. Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration and prompt allowance of all pending claims.

Applicant does not concede that the subject matter encompassed by the claims prior to this Response is unpatentable over the art cited by the Office Action. While several distinctions have been noted over the art of record, Applicant notes that there may be several other limitations that are neither taught nor suggested by the art of record. Applicant expressly reserves all rights and arguments with respect to distinctions not explicitly noted herein. In addition, to the extent that amendments included herein constitute a narrowing of the claims, such narrowing of the claims should not be construed as an admission as to the merits of the prior rejections. Indeed, Applicant traverses the rejections and preserves all rights and arguments. To the extent that any particular statement or argument by the Office in the pending Office Action has not been
explicitly addressed herein, the same should not be construed as an acquiescence or admission by the Applicant that such statements or arguments by the Office are accurate and proper.
Please charge any additional fees or credit any overpayment to deposit account number 50-1778. The Examiner is invited to telephone the below-signed attorney to discuss this application.
